children: The following diagrams are featured in this topic:
This process generates work instructions for work requests from

Step 1: The system organizes the appropriate work creation master records 
 in priority order.

The system determines which records it needs to retrieve, based 
 on the process that requested work creation. The process determines why 
 work creation was initiated. On each work creation record, the system 
 checks the

The system organizes the appropriate work creation master records 
 based on priority number.

After the system determines 
 which records can be applied to the work requests, the system organizes 
 them in priority order. The priority number is defined on the work 
 creation master record. The lower the priority number, the sooner the 
 record is used to process work requests.

Step 2: The system compares each work request to the first eligible 
 work creation master record.

Based on priority, the system selects the first creation master 
 record that it will compare to the work requests.

The system references the work criteria record associated with this 
 work creation master. The work criteria record defines which work requests 
 can be processed using the work creation master record.

If the request does meet the 
 criteria defined 
 on the work criteria record, the system will associate it with 
 the work creation master record. This request will not be reviewed by 
 the next work creation master: it is 'reserved'. The system will compare 
 the remaining requests to this work creation master record.

If the request does not meet 
 the criteria 
 defined on the work criteria record, 
 the system temporarily holds the request. It retrieves the next request 
 and attempts to process it using this work creation master 
 record. After the system has processed through all of the requests, it 
 will compare the 'declined' request to the next work creation master record.

Step 3: The system organizes the requests based on the order by attributes 
 on the work criteria record.

The system checks the attributes defined on the 
 Order By Tab on the Work Criteria Record. It organizes the requests based 
 on the values defined on this tab.

For example, assume the tab contains the following value: Shipment 
 ID, Ascending Order. The system will organize the requests in shipment 
 ID order, with the lowest ID number first.

If multiple values are defined on the tab, the 
 system will further organize the requests within the first attribute. 
 For example, in the screen diagram below, each of the requests would be 
 organized in Shipment ID order, ascending. So, all requests for Shipment 
 ID 1 would be ordered before all requests for Shipment ID 2. Within each 
 Shipment ID, the details are further organized in pick location order, 
 ascending. So, requests for location 100-100-001 are ordered before requests 
 for location 100-100-002. Finally, within each location, the requests 
 are organized in item number order, ascending.
Note that this screen diagram is from the Order By Tab on the Work Criteria Window.

Step 4: The system assigns instruction numbers to each detail and generates 
 work units.

The system processes through the detail records in the order created 
 during Step 3.

Each request becomes a detail. Each detail is assigned a work instruction 
 number. This is an internal number that identifies the detail to the system.

The system determines which estimated work rate 
 record it can apply to each instruction. It uses this record to calculate 
 how long it will take an employee to process the instruction.
Step 5: The system creates work units.

The system references the work creation master 
 record to determine how to create the work unit. Note that when the work is replenishment work created out of the 
 wave process,          and the "Wave 
 Replen Work Type" setting (on the Work System Values Window) is activated, 
 the system will use this special replenishment work type instead of using 
 the work type as defined on the work creation master.

When the system reaches the work unit break, it creates a work unit. 
 The work unit is assigned an instruction number. The work unit groups 
 together all instructions that will be assigned to one employee.

If the Auto Print Checkbox on the Work Creation Master Window is 
 selected and this work unit was created for an outbound process, the system 
 will print the pick list as soon as the work unit is created.

For order picking, work units are often created 
 at the order or shipment number level. For batch picking, work units are 
 often created at the pick location level.

The work execution process occurs when employees obtain the product 
 required to fullfill customers' shipment requests. The work units processed 
 during work execution were generated during work creation. Work that is not executed on an RF device is typically completed from 
 pick lists. The procedures below provide a general method for executing 
 Non-RF work; since system intervention is minimal, the actual procedures 
 are based on your business practices.
Step 1: The system generates the pick lists.

Pick lists are generated at the work unit level. To system references 
 the work criteria record to determine which instructions are included 
 in the pick list.
The following values are defined on the pick list:

Step 2: A manager distributes the 
 pick lists to the appropriate personnel.

Employees will obtain product from the From Locations and deliver 
 it to the To Locations. If applicable, they will use a time/date stamp 
 to indicate when product was picked and putaway.

Step 3: An administrator confirms 
 the work activity on the Work Insight Screen.

After the employee has processed the work on the pick list, he/she 
 will deliver the pick list to the data administrator responsible for entering 
 work activity in the system. Note: The user and warehouse must have access to a work profile that supports the work type and work zones on the work instruction.

The data administrator will use the Work Insight Screen to indicate 
 what work activity occurred on the floor. He/she will complete the following 
 activities:
Identify the person who processed the work unit.

Identify when the product was picked and putaway in the Start 
 Time/Date and End Time/Date Fields (if a time/date stamp was used).

If appropriate identify why a short pick or other irregular 
 activity occur.

Once the work is confirmed, the system will change its status to 
 Ready for Packing.

If you have created additional status between 
 In Picking and Ready for Packing, the unit will change to the next appropriate 
 status.

The work execution process occurs when employees obtain the product 
 required to fulfill customers' shipment requests. The work units processed 
 during work execution were generated during work creation.

Step 1: The employee signs on to an RF device. The system determines 
 which work profile to associate with the employee

How an employee can work is determined by the work profile record associated 
 with his/her user sign on. When the employee signs on to an RF device (and 
 chooses the Work function), the system will determine how he/she should 
 process work. The system uses the following process to select the appropriate 
 work profile:

First, the system will reference the employee's 
 user profile. If a work profile is defined as the "default work profile"on 
 his/her user profile, the system will assign this profile to the user. 
 The system will not continue to step B.

However, if the employee's user profile does not have a work profile associated 
 with it, the system will prompt with work profiles that are user and warehouse authorized.
Step 2: The system retrieves the user's existing work profile detail record(s)

The system can only assign those work instructions 
 that match a detail record on the user's assigned work profile. It looks for the following 
 fit:

- The work instruction's work type must match the work type on the 
 work profile.

- The work instruction's work zone must accept the equipment type defined 
 on the work profile detail record.

Note that if none of the detail records match the work instructions, the system 
 will display a message requiring the employee to obtain work from a supervisor.

Step 3: The system will determine the method of work initiation: the system 
 or the user?

If the system 
 should initiate work, the user will scan the nearest location barcode. 
 The system will assign the work unit closest to this location. The employee 
 will identify the work unit with an arbitrary barcode.

System-Directed Work Unit Selection: If the from location (where the system assigned you a work unit) is eligible for system-directed work unit selection, then the system will display an additional initiation screen. This allows you to choose the work unit you wish to execute.  All the work unit validations for this system-directed work unit selection screen are identical to the validations that the system performs when initiating work with the user-directed initiation screen (such as the work unit cannot be closed, cannot be active, etc).

If the user should 
 initiate work, he/she will determine which work unit should be 
 processed first. He/she will scan the work unit's barcode, usually from 
 the pick list generated during work creation. Note that "Group user" work can also be initiated, which 
 allows you to consolidate container picks. For more detailed information on executing group-user work, see the topic
If starting receipt putaway work from RF for a receipt container and the To location on the work instruction is the receiving pre-locate location, then the system will relocate the receipt container.
Step 4: The system will assign the appropriate work unit to the employee

Within the work 
 unit, instructions are assigned based on the From Assign Method 
 Field on the work profile detail record.

Within the work 
 unit, the system assigns work summaries, not work instructions, 
 to the user.

Step 5: The system applies any special handling constraints to the 
 work unit; system displays instruction/quantity to be picked

The system references the Work Special Handling Constraints Window to identify 
 unique handling requirements for this work unit. A special handling constraints 
 record determines the following:

When additional handling constraints are required. 
 These constraints can be set for any of the following characteristics:
- Per User Profile / Work Zone / Work Type

If constraints are required, the system will determine 
 what type of constraint is used. Any combination of the following constraints 
 can be used, including:

- Employee must identify the pick location by scanning the location 
 number .
- Employee must verify the item quantity that he/she is processing.
- A maximum quantity pickup set to minimize breakage or loss.
- The ability to override the location, lot, or license plate data for specific work instructions.

System then displays the work unit's first/next 
 work instruction, or the quantity to be picked (after performing a partial 
 pick action), in the Pick Confirmation Window.
Step 6: The user picks the product

Next, the user picks the product, and enters the appropriate data into 
 the RF device.

If the user performs 
 a complete pick, the system will process the pick.

If the user performs 
 a short pick, the system will reject the quantity that was short 
 picked, and decrement the short picked quantity from the On Hand quantity 
 at the location.

If the user performs 
 a partial pick, the system will delete the remaining quantity from 
 the work instruction, and close it, if the "Close on Partial Pick" 
 checkbox (in Work Special Handling Window) is selected. If not, the system 
 would keep the instruction open so the remainder could be picked later. 
 Note that the "partial pick and close" action is only available 
 for RF replenishment and work order picks if it is defined to do so in 
 the Work Special Handling Window. If you are partial picking into a tote or shipping container, the system 
 will return you to the same pick again after a partial pick, displaying 
 the remaining quantity that is yet to be picked. The system will repeat 
 this action until the whole quantity is picked. This is helpful if you 
 cannot fit a complete pick into one tote/container.

If the user performs 
 an over pick, the system will increment the transaction quantity, 
 and process the pick as a complete pick. Note that this action is only 
 available for RF replenishment and work order picks if it is defined to 
 do so in the Work Special Handling Window.
After the pick processing is completed:

The system will 
 display the work unit's first/next putaway instruction.

The system will 
 automatically putaway the work unit's item, if the Select After 
 Putaway Checkbox was selected on the current user's work profile record. 
 This would bypass having to manually putaway the item. Typically, this 
 setting would be used when you are picking directly into shipping containers 
 (but you can use it in any work scenario).

The user will putaway the item quantity at the appropriate location. Note that if your work profile is defined to putaway into shipping containers, and you are putting away to a put-to-store location or the shipping dock, you will need to provide the container ID that you are putting into. Also, if this is a new container, you will need to indicate the container type. After the user performs the putaway action on the item, the system 
 will putaway the quantity in the specified location. If the user's work profile 
 indicates that they should nest container(s) after putaway, the system 
 will display a screen to perform this action. The system will also check 
 to see if there is any more putaway to be completed for this work unit. 
 If there is, the next instruction will be displayed. If not, the system 
 will check to see if there is any more work for this work profile detail.

If multiple values are defined on the tab, the 
 system will further organize the requests within the first attribute. 
 For example, in the screen diagram below, each of the requests would be 
 organized in Shipment ID order, ascending. So, all requests for Shipment 
 ID 1 would be ordered before all requests for Shipment ID 2. Within each 
 Shipment ID, the details are further organized in pick location order, 
 ascending. So, requests for location 100-100-001 are ordered before requests 
 for location 100-100-002. Finally, within each location, the requests 
 are organized in item number order, ascending.

        

        
 

        

            
            
        

        
 

        
Note that this screen diagram is from the Order By Tab on the Work Criteria Window.

        
 

        
 

        
Step 4: The system assigns instruction numbers to each detail and generates 
 work units.

        

            

                
The system processes through the detail records in the order created 
 during Step 3.

                
 

            

            

                
Each request becomes a detail. Each detail is assigned a work instruction 
 number. This is an internal number that identifies the detail to the system.

                
 

            

            
The system determines which estimated work rate 
 record it can apply to each instruction. It uses this record to calculate 
 how long it will take an employee to process the instruction.

        

        
 

        
Step 5: The system creates work units.

        

            
The system references the work creation master 
 record to determine how to create the work unit. Note that when the work is replenishment work created out of the 
 wave process,          and the "Wave 
 Replen Work Type" setting (on the Work System Values Window) is activated, 
 the system will use this special replenishment work type instead of using 
 the work type as defined on the work creation master.

 

            

                
When the system reaches the work unit break, it creates a work unit. 
 The work unit is assigned an instruction number. The work unit groups 
 together all instructions that will be assigned to one employee.

                
 

            

            

                
If the Auto Print Checkbox on the Work Creation Master Window is 
 selected and this work unit was created for an outbound process, the system 
 will print the pick list as soon as the work unit is created.

                
 

            

            
For order picking, work units are often created 
 at the order or shipment number level. For batch picking, work units are 
 often created at the pick location level.

        

        
 

        


        
  

        
 

        
Work Execution Flow Diagram...

        
 

        

            
        

        
 

        
 

        
Non-RF Work Execution

        
The work execution process occurs when employees obtain the product 
 required to fullfill customers' shipment requests. The work units processed 
 during work execution were generated during work creation. Work that is not executed on an RF device is typically completed from 
 pick lists. The procedures below provide a general method for executing 
 Non-RF work; since system intervention is minimal, the actual procedures 
 are based on your business practices.

        
 

        
 

        
Step 1: The system generates the pick lists.

        

            

                
Pick lists are generated at the work unit level. To system references 
 the work criteria record to determine which instructions are included 
 in the pick list.

                
 

            

            

                
The following values are defined on the pick list:

                
 

            

            

                

                    
Work Unit Number

                    
 

                

                

                    
Team (if applicable)

                    
 

                

                

                    
From Zone

                    
 

                

                

                    
From Location

                    
 

                

                

                    
To Zone

                    
 

                

                

                    
To Location

                    
 

                

                

                    
Item # / Description

                    
 

                

                

                    
Quantity

                    
 

                

                

                    
Order Number

                    
 

                

                
Order Line Number.

            

            
 

        

        
Step 2: A manager distributes the 
 pick lists to the appropriate personnel.

        

            

                
Employees will obtain product from the From Locations and deliver 
 it to the To Locations. If applicable, they will use a time/date stamp 
 to indicate when product was picked and putaway.

                
 

            

        

        
Step 3: An administrator confirms 
 the work activity on the Work Insight Screen.

        

            

                
After the employee has processed the work on the pick list, he/she 
 will deliver the pick list to the data administrator responsible for entering 
 work activity in the system. Note: The user and warehouse must have access to a work profile that supports the work type and work zones on the work instruction.

                
 

            

            

                
The data administrator will use the Work Insight Screen to indicate 
 what work activity occurred on the floor. He/she will complete the following 
 activities:

                
 

            

            

                

                    
Identify the person who processed the work unit.

                    
 

                

                

                    
Identify when the product was picked and putaway in the Start 
 Time/Date and End Time/Date Fields (if a time/date stamp was used).

                    
 

                

                

                    
Identify the quantity picked.

                    
 

                

                

                    
If appropriate identify why a short pick or other irregular 
 activity occur.

                    
 

                

                
Confirm the work.

            

            
 

            

                
Once the work is confirmed, the system will change its status to 
 Ready for Packing.

                
 

            

            

                
If you have created additional status between 
 In Picking and Ready for Packing, the unit will change to the next appropriate 
 status.

            

        

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
RF Work Execution Flow Diagram...

        
 

        

            
        

        
 

        
 

        
RF Work Execution

        
The work execution process occurs when employees obtain the product 
 required to fulfill customers' shipment requests. The work units processed 
 during work execution were generated during work creation.

        
 

        
 

        
Step 1: The employee signs on to an RF device. The system determines 
 which work profile to associate with the employee

        
How an employee can work is determined by the work profile record associated 
 with his/her user sign on. When the employee signs on to an RF device (and 
 chooses the Work function), the system will determine how he/she should 
 process work. The system uses the following process to select the appropriate 
 work profile:

        

            
First, the system will reference the employee's 
 user profile. If a work profile is defined as the "default work profile"on 
 his/her user profile, the system will assign this profile to the user. 
 The system will not continue to step B. 





            
However, if the employee's user profile does not have a work profile associated 
 with it, the system will prompt with work profiles that are user and warehouse authorized. 

        

        
 

        
Step 2: The system retrieves the user's existing work profile detail record(s)

        

            
The system can only assign those work instructions 
 that match a detail record on the user's assigned work profile. It looks for the following 
 fit:



- The work instruction's work type must match the work type on the 
 work profile.



- The work instruction's work zone must accept the equipment type defined 
 on the work profile detail record.

        

        
Note that if none of the detail records match the work instructions, the system 
 will display a message requiring the employee to obtain work from a supervisor.

        
 

        
 

        
Step 3: The system will determine the method of work initiation: the system 
 or the user?

        

            
If the system 
 should initiate work, the user will scan the nearest location barcode. 
 The system will assign the work unit closest to this location. The employee 
 will identify the work unit with an arbitrary barcode.



System-Directed Work Unit Selection: If the from location (where the system assigned you a work unit) is eligible for system-directed work unit selection, then the system will display an additional initiation screen. This allows you to choose the work unit you wish to execute.  All the work unit validations for this system-directed work unit selection screen are identical to the validations that the system performs when initiating work with the user-directed initiation screen (such as the work unit cannot be closed, cannot be active, etc).





            
If the user should 
 initiate work, he/she will determine which work unit should be 
 processed first. He/she will scan the work unit's barcode, usually from 
 the pick list generated during work creation. Note that "Group user" work can also be initiated, which 
 allows you to consolidate container picks. For more detailed information on executing group-user work, see the topic Processing RF Work (Group User section)





            

                
If starting receipt putaway work from RF for a receipt container and the To location on the work instruction is the receiving pre-locate location, then the system will relocate the receipt container.

            

        

        
  

        
Step 4: The system will assign the appropriate work unit to the employee

        

            
Within the work 
 unit, instructions are assigned based on the From Assign Method 
 Field on the work profile detail record.





            
Within the work 
 unit, the system assigns work summaries, not work instructions, 
 to the user.

        

        
 

        
Step 5: The system applies any special handling constraints to the 
 work unit; system displays instruction/quantity to be picked

        
The system references the Work Special Handling Constraints Window to identify 
 unique handling requirements for this work unit. A special handling constraints 
 record determines the following:

        

            
When additional handling constraints are required. 
 These constraints can be set for any of the following characteristics:



- Per Item / Company



- Per Account / Company



- Per User Profile / Work Zone / Work Type





            
If constraints are required, the system will determine 
 what type of constraint is used. Any combination of the following constraints 
 can be used, including:



- Employee must identify the pick location by scanning the location 
 number .



- Employee must verify the item quantity that he/she is processing.



- A maximum quantity pickup set to minimize breakage or loss.



- The ability to override the location, lot, or license plate data for specific work instructions.





            
System then displays the work unit's first/next 
 work instruction, or the quantity to be picked (after performing a partial 
 pick action), in the Pick Confirmation Window.

        

        
 

        
 

        
Step 6: The user picks the product

        
Next, the user picks the product, and enters the appropriate data into 
 the RF device.

        

            
If the user performs 
 a complete pick, the system will process the pick.





            
If the user performs 
 a short pick, the system will reject the quantity that was short 
 picked, and decrement the short picked quantity from the On Hand quantity 
 at the location.





            
If the user performs 
 a partial pick, the system will delete the remaining quantity from 
 the work instruction, and close it, if the "Close on Partial Pick" 
 checkbox (in Work Special Handling Window) is selected. If not, the system 
 would keep the instruction open so the remainder could be picked later. 
 Note that the "partial pick and close" action is only available 
 for RF replenishment and work order picks if it is defined to do so in 
 the Work Special Handling Window. If you are partial picking into a tote or shipping container, the system 
 will return you to the same pick again after a partial pick, displaying 
 the remaining quantity that is yet to be picked. The system will repeat 
 this action until the whole quantity is picked. This is helpful if you 
 cannot fit a complete pick into one tote/container.





            
If the user performs 
 an over pick, the system will increment the transaction quantity, 
 and process the pick as a complete pick. Note that this action is only 
 available for RF replenishment and work order picks if it is defined to 
 do so in the Work Special Handling Window.

        

        
After the pick processing is completed:

        

            
The system will 
 display the work unit's first/next putaway instruction.



OR





            
The system will 
 automatically putaway the work unit's item, if the Select After 
 Putaway Checkbox was selected on the current user's work profile record. 
 This would bypass having to manually putaway the item. Typically, this 
 setting would be used when you are picking directly into shipping containers 
 (but you can use it in any work scenario).

        

        
 

        
 

        
Step 7: The user performs putaway.

        
The user will putaway the item quantity at the appropriate location. Note that if your work profile is defined to putaway into shipping containers, and you are putting away to a put-to-store location or the shipping dock, you will need to provide the container ID that you are putting into. Also, if this is a new container, you will need to indicate the container type. After the user performs the putaway action on the item, the system 
 will putaway the quantity in the specified location. If the user's work profile 
 indicates that they should nest container(s) after putaway, the system 
 will display a screen to perform this action. The system will also check 
 to see if there is any more putaway to be completed for this work unit. 
 If there is, the next instruction will be displayed. If not, the system 
 will check to see if there is any more work for this work profile detail.

        
 

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
Picking Management Flow Diagram...

        
 

        

            
        

        
 

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
System Directed Work Flow...

 in priority order.

 work creation master record.

 on the work criteria record.

Step 4: The system assigns instruction numbers to each detail and generates 
 work units.

 the work activity on the Work Insight Screen.

 or the user?
